what_its_for: Clobetasol is a very strong steroid cream, ointment, gel, or foam used on your skin to reduce redness, swelling, itching, and irritation caused by certain skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, and other inflammatory skin problems.
how_to_take: Wash your hands before and after applying clobetasol. Apply a thin layer only to the affected area of skin as directed by your doctor. Gently rub it in. Do not cover the treated area with a bandage or wrap unless your doctor tells you to. Do not apply it to your face, underarms, or groin unless specifically told to do so by your doctor. Avoid getting it in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Do not use more than directed — using too much or for too long can cause serious side effects.
dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area 1 to 2 times per day, or exactly as your doctor prescribes. Do not use clobetasol for more than 2 consecutive weeks without talking to your doctor. Do not use more than 50 grams of cream or ointment per week.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store clobetasol at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. Do not freeze it. Keep the cap or lid tightly closed and keep it out of reach of children. For foam products, keep away from open flame or heat as they are flammable.
what_to_avoid: Do not use clobetasol on your face, armpits, or groin unless your doctor specifically instructs you to. Avoid getting it in your eyes — if contact occurs, rinse well with water. Do not use it on broken, infected, or open skin without your doctor's approval. Do not use more than prescribed or for longer than recommended. Avoid wrapping or covering the treated skin tightly unless directed, as this can increase absorption and cause side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you experience: skin thinning, stretch marks, or unusual bruising at the application site; redness, burning, or irritation that gets worse; signs of skin infection such as increased warmth, pus, or pain; skin lightening (change in skin color); unusual weight gain, swelling, or a round, puffy face; increased thirst or urination; or if your condition does not improve after 2 weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in itching and redness within a few days of starting treatment. Full improvement of your skin condition may take 1 to 2 weeks. If you do not see improvement after 2 weeks, contact your doctor. Do not use it for longer than recommended without checking with your doctor.
special_populations: Children: Clobetasol should be used with extra caution in children because they absorb more of the medication through their skin, which increases the risk of side effects. It should not be used in children under 12 years old. Use the smallest amount needed for the shortest time possible. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using clobetasol. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. If you are breastfeeding, avoid applying clobetasol to the chest or breast area to prevent your baby from accidentally ingesting it. Elderly patients: Elderly individuals may have thinner skin and should use this medication carefully to reduce the risk of skin thinning and bruising.
